title: Germany – Electric buses – Beschaffung von bis zu 4 Niederflursolobussen und 1 Niederflurgelenkbus mit Elektroantrieb
description: Die Auftraggeberin beabsichtigt die Beschaffung von insgesamt bis zu 4 Niederflursolobussen und einem Niederflurgelenkbus (5 Busse) mit Elektroantrieb zur Elektrifizierung der Busflotte. Die technischen Anforderungen und weiteren Leistungsge-gen-stände sind dem Lastenheft (Anlage 6) zu entnehmen. Der Einsatz der Elektrobusse soll im öffentlichen Personennahverkehr erfolgen. Die abschließende Planung, ob Elektrobusse benötigt werden, wie viele Elektrobusse benötigt werden und in welchem Verkehr sie eingesetzt werden, konnte bisher nicht erfolgen. Aufgrund zuwendungsrechtlicher Fristen konnte die abschließende Pla-nung nicht abgewartet werden. Daher schreibt die Auftraggeberin eine Rahmenvereinbarung für die Elektrobusse aus (vgl. Anlage 8 § 2). Die Auftraggeberin wird, abhängig vom Bedarf, 0 Solobusse bis maximal 4 Solobusse und 0 bis einen Gelenkbus aus der Rahmenvereinbarung abrufen. Eine Abnahmeverpflichtung der Auftragnehmerin besteht aus der Rahmenvereinbarung nicht. Spätester Liefertermin für die Fahrzeuge ist der 31.3.2028.

title: Kaupin yliopistollinen sosiaali- ja terveysasema pääurakka
description: Kaupin yliopistollinen sosiaali- ja terveysasema pääurakka Tämän hankintailmoituksen tarjouspyyntöön on päivitetty aiemman tarjouspyynnön virheellinen kirjaus tarjoajan liikevaihtovaatimuksesta. Samalla tarjouspyynnön määräaikoja on jatkettu 1 viikolla tarjouspyynnössä ilmoitetun mukaisesti. Tekniseen laskenta-aineistoon ei ole tehty muutoksia. Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialue valmistelee Kaupin yliopistollisen sosiaali- ja terveysaseman uudisrakennushanketta Tampereen yliopistollisen sairaalan Kaupin kampusalueelle. Kaupin yliopistollisen sote-aseman uudisrakennus (uusi C-rakennus) on n. 15 000 brm2:n (urakoinnin laajuus laskenta-asiakirjojen mukaan) laajuinen rakennus, johon sijoitetaan mm. terveysaseman vastaanottopalvelut, aikuisten sekä lasten- ja nuorten mielenterveys- ja päihdepalvelut, työikäisten sosiaalityö ja perheohjaus, avokuntoutus, suun terveydenhuolto, äitiys- ja lastenneuvola sekä kehitystä tukevat palvelut. Uusi C-rakennus rakennetaan Taysin Kaupin kampukselle nykyisten purettavien TAMKin rakennusten paikalle. Vanhat rakennukset puretaan ennen uudisrakennuksen urakan käynnistymistä. Uusi C-rakennus kytketään tunnelilla sairaala-alueen tunneliverkostoon ja ilmasillalla sairaalakampukseen sekä TAMKin olemassa olevaan ilmasiltaan. Hankkeen urakkamuoto on jaettu urakka. Tällä hankintailmoituksella haetaan hankkeelle rakennusurakoitsijaa, joka toimii hankkeessa myös pääurakoitsijana ja lainsäädännön tarkoittamana päätoteuttajana. Rakennustyöt on suunniteltu urakka-asiakirjojen mukaan alkavaksi ensisijaisesti kesäkuussa 2027, kuitenkin viimeistään syyskuussa 2027. Rakennusaikaa varataan 23 kuukautta. Hankkeen sivu-urakoitsijoita (putkiurakkaan, ilmanvaihtourakkaan, sammutusjärjestelmäurakkaan ja sähköurakkaan) haetaan toisella erillisellä hankintailmoituksella. Rakennusautomaatiourakoitsijana tulee toimimaan Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueen puitesopimuskumppani. Tarjouslaskenta-aikaa annetaan noin kolme kuukautta.,

title: Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Bimekizumab, ATC L04AC21 für die Zeit 01.10.2026 - 31.03.2027
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Bimekizumab, ATC L04AC21, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.10.2026 in Kraft und endet am 31.03.2027. Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

title: Beschaffung von bis zu 4 Niederflursolobussen und 1 Niederflurgelenkbus mit Elektroantrieb
description: Die Auftraggeberin beabsichtigt die Beschaffung von insgesamt bis zu 4 Niederflursolobussen und einem Niederflurgelenkbus (5 Busse) mit Elektroantrieb zur Elektrifizierung der Busflotte. Die technischen Anforderungen und weiteren Leistungsge-gen-stände sind dem Lastenheft (Anlage 6) zu entnehmen. Der Einsatz der Elektrobusse soll im öffentlichen Personennahverkehr erfolgen. Die abschließende Planung, ob Elektrobusse benötigt werden, wie viele Elektrobusse benötigt werden und in welchem Verkehr sie eingesetzt werden, konnte bisher nicht erfolgen. Aufgrund zuwendungsrechtlicher Fristen konnte die abschließende Pla-nung nicht abgewartet werden. Daher schreibt die Auftraggeberin eine Rahmenvereinbarung für die Elektrobusse aus (vgl. Anlage 8 § 2). Die Auftraggeberin wird, abhängig vom Bedarf, 0 Solobusse bis maximal 4 Solobusse und 0 bis einen Gelenkbus aus der Rahmenvereinbarung abrufen. Eine Abnahmeverpflichtung der Auftragnehmerin besteht aus der Rahmenvereinbarung nicht. Spätester Liefertermin für die Fahrzeuge ist der 31.3.2028.

title: Component Rebuild Shop at Letterkenny Army Depot
description: ----NOTICE OF CHANGES --- The solicitation number for this contract will be W912DR26RA034. Links to the correct SAM.GOV solicitation and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module for the subject requirement will be posted to this presolicitation. The publicized release date for W912DR26RA034 solicitation is anticipated on/about 18 March 2026.---- THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP). No proposals are being solicited or accepted at this time. The Government is not liable for any costs incurred by interested parties in response to this notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore District, intends to issue a solicitation for the design and construction of a new Component Rebuild Shop at Letterkenny Army Depot, Pennsylvania. This solicitation will be competed on an unrestricted basis. The Government intends to award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract using a Two-Phase Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) approach aligning with selection procedures outlined in the Federal Acquisition Regulations. The scope includes demolition of an existing 16,700 GSF building and construction of a new facility containing vehicle repair bays, administrative offices, building support areas, and extensive site work including utilities, paving, and parking. The new facility of approximately 72,000 gross square feet (GSF) to support depot-level maintenance for various ground support and guided missile systems. The anticipated period of performance is 1,095 calendar days from Notice To Proceed. Pursuant to the nature of Design-Build procurement, the Government will not provide detailed construction plans. The successful offeror will be solely responsible for developing the design solution and for the professional integrity of the final design. Phase One (Request for Qualifications): The Government anticipates issuing the Phase One Request For Qualifications (RFQ) on or about 13 March 2026. This phase will be a qualifications-based competition to select a shortlist of the most highly qualified offerors. Phase Two: Shortlisted offerors will be issued a draft Request For Proposals (RFP) outlining the technical requirements for the project and will be invited to a series of one-on-one proprietary meetings in order to develop the final scope of work within the budget ceiling of $78,000,000. Upon completion of these meetings, a final RFP will be issued. Phase Two evaluations will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15, with an award based on a best value determination. This action will be subject to the Buy American statute. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. NOTICE: This project is anticipated to have a Project Labor Agreement requirement. USACE requests any contractors who would like to provide any further feedback related to the DBtB acquisition strategy and any potential impacts, positive or otherwise to provide them via email to the POC listed in this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Component Rebuild Shop at Letterkenny Army Depot
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP). No proposals are being solicited or accepted at this time. The Government is not liable for any costs incurred by interested parties in response to this notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore District, intends to issue a solicitation for the design and construction of a new Component Rebuild Shop at Letterkenny Army Depot, Pennsylvania. The new facility of approximately 72,000 gross square feet (GSF) to support depot-level maintenance for various ground support and guided missile systems. The scope includes demolition of an existing 16,700 GSF building and construction of a new facility containing vehicle repair bays, administrative offices, building support areas, and extensive site work including utilities, paving, and parking. The estimated magnitude of this construction project is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000 with a Construction Cost limitation of $78,000,000. The anticipated period of performance is 1,095 calendar days from Notice To Proceed. Pursuant to the nature of Design-Build procurement, the Government will not provide detailed construction plans. The successful offeror will be solely responsible for developing the design solution and for the professional integrity of the final design. The Government intends to award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract using the Two-Phase Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) aligning with selection procedures outlined in Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) subpart 36.101. Phase One (Request for Qualifications): The Government anticipates issuing the Phase One RFQ on or about 2 March 2026. This phase will be a qualifications-based competition to select a shortlist of the most highly qualified offerors. Phase Two: Shortlisted offerors will be issued a draft RFP outlining the technical requirements for the project and will be invited to a series of one-on-one proprietary meetings in order to develop the final scope of work within the budget ceiling of $78,000,000. Upon completion of these meetings, a final RFP will be issued. Phase Two evaluations will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15, with an award based on a best value determination. This action will be subject to the Buy American statute. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. NOTICE: This project is anticipated to have a Project Labor Agreement requirement. USACE requests any contractors who would like to provide any further feedback related to the DBtB acquisition strategy and any potential impacts, positive or otherwise to provide them via email to the POC listed in this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Bulgaria – Pharmaceutical products – ДСП Доставка на лекарствени продукти за УМБАЛ „Св. Иван Рилски“ ЕАД
description: ДСП - Доставка на лекарствени продукти съгасно първоначално планиран спектър /част от документацията за участие/ с посочено естество на продуктите, прогнозна стойност, както и посочено прогнозно количество. Първоначално планиранираният спектър може да бъде частично изменен, както и да се добавят нови продукти в хода на динамичната система. Количествата са ориентировъчни. Възложителят не e длъжен да изкупи посочените в спектъра количества. Одобрените кандидати могат да подадат оферта за една или повече единици, както и могат да не подадат оферта. ДСП функционира на два етапа: Първи етап - събиране на заявления за участие и Втори етап - събиране на оферти по конкретни покани. Разглеждането на първоначалните заявления за участие ще се извърши в срок до 15 работни дни от крайният срок за подаване на заявления. Покана за конкретна поръчка няма да бъде обявявана преди да бъдат разгледани всички заявления. Офертите ще бъдат класирани от програма, която ще е достъпна и безплатна за всички кандидати. Осигурен е неограничен, пълен и пряк достъп до документацията за обществената поръчка през целия срок на действие на ДСП. ДСП ще функционира в рамките на три години, а именно в рамките на три години възложителят може да отправя покани до допуснатите кандидати за събиране на оферти за доставка на медицински изделия включени в първоначално планираният спектър или извън него. Слючените договори ще са със срок на действие: две години.

title: Netherlands – Social work services without accommodation – Inburgering: Participatie en MAP
description: Deze opdracht richt zich op het bevorderen van de participatie van de inburgeraar met als hoogste streven instroom in betaald werk. Afhankelijk van de afstand tot de arbeidsmarkt wordt ingezet op: • Maatschappelijke participatie (trede 0 t/m 4 op de participatieladder) • Of ontwikkelen naar werk (trede 5 en 6 op de participatieladder). • Aanvullend hierop oriënteren inburgeraars zich binnen de Module Arbeidsmarkt en Participatie (MAP) op participatie en werk en krijgen zij inzicht in de Nederlandse arbeidsmarkt en hun eigen mogelijkheden en kansen. Voor de participatieopdracht wordt 75% van de dienstverlening uitgevoerd door Diamant-Groep/KikMaat (inbesteding) en 25% via deze aanbesteding in de markt gezet. De gemeente streeft naar spiegelcontracten, waarbij beide delen inhoudelijk zoveel mogelijk gelijk worden ingericht en deelnemers volgens een vaste verdeelsleutel worden verdeeld. De Overeenkomsten wordt aangegaan voor een initiële looptijd van 3 jaar, m.i.v. 1-1-2028. Omvang

title: Netherlands – Social work services without accommodation – Inburgering: Leerroutes 18 tot en met 26 jaar en Onderwijsroute MBO
description: Deze opdracht richt zich op taal als basis voor inburgering. Deze opdracht is opgebouwd uit twee percelen: • Opdracht 2A: jongvolwassenen (18 tot en met 26 jaar). Focus op startkwalificatie, waarin de B1-route en Z-route, beide in combinatie met Entree-onderwijs, worden aangeboden. • Opdracht 2C: onderwijsroute MBO. De Overeenkomsten wordt aangegaan voor een initiële looptijd van 4 jaar, m.i.v. 1-1-2028. Er wordt door gemeente Tilburg samengewerkt met de volgende gemeenten: • Dongen • Goirle, • Heusden, • Hilvarenbeek, • Loon op Zand • Oisterwijk • Waalwijk • Alphen-Chaam, Baarle-Nassau en Gilze en Rijen via het ABG-samenwerkingsverband Omvang

title: Netherlands – Social work services without accommodation – Inburgering: Warm Welkom, Maatschappelijk Begeleiding en Participatieverklaringstraject
description: Deze opdracht richt zich op een goede landing van inburgeraars. Warm Welkom ziet op de eerste opvang en begeleiding direct na de huisvesting in de gemeente, zodat inburgeraars snel hun weg vinden naar voorzieningen en kunnen starten met hun inburgering. Maatschappelijke begeleiding richt zich op het ondersteunen van inburgeraars bij het vergroten van hun zelfredzaamheid, het regelen van praktische zaken en het bevorderen van participatie in de Nederlandse samenleving. Het Participatieverklaringstraject (PVT) richt zich op het laten kennismaken van inburgeraars met de Nederlandse samenleving, de kernwaarden van de Nederlandse rechtsstaat, de Nederlandse normen en waarden en de spelregels van de samenleving, waarna zij de participatieverklaring ondertekenen. title: Ireland – Tree-maintenance services – DCC Multi-Party Framework Agreement for the Provision of Tree Care Services
description: The Framework Agreement covers the provision of tree surgery services to ensure that all trees under the care and management of Dublin City Council, including street trees and trees growing in parks and open spaces, are maintained in accordance with recognized arboricultural best practices and industry standards. The scope of services to be delivered under this Framework generally includes, but is not limited to, tree pruning operations such as crown reduction, limb pruning, crown lifting, and crown thinning, as well as tree felling and stump removal works. All services are intended to support the safe, sustainable, and effective management of the Council’s tree stock while promoting public safety, tree health, and environmental quality across the city. This Framework Agreement has been established to appoint suitably qualified and experienced economic operators who will be eligible to compete for individual work packages. The framework will be for 4 years. The framework will primarily be used by the Parks and Landscape Services Division, but may also be used by other divisions of Dublin City Council.. description: The goal of this solicitation is to accelerate the development, adaptation, evaluation, demonstration, and adoption of innovative technologies that improve the safety and health of mine workers across coal, metal, nonmetal, stone, sand, and gravel mining operations. NIOSH seeks applied research and technology-development efforts that have a credible pathway toward practical implementation in surface or underground mines. Of particular interest are projects that: 1) Advance promising prototype technologies toward mine-ready solutions, including final development, adaptation to challenging mining environments, modification to meet applicable permissibility requirements, and demonstration at mine sites. 2) Adapt technologies successfully used in other industries for mining applications, including necessary redesign, ruggedization, integration, permissibility modifications, performance evaluation, and in-mine demonstration. 3) Evaluate emerging or candidate technologies to determine their potential to improve mine worker safety and health, identify technical or operational barriers to implementation, and develop approaches for overcoming those barriers. 4) Facilitate adoption of mature safety and health technologies that are available but have not achieved widespread mining-industry implementation. Activities may include establishing initial operational capability through mine demonstrations, evaluating technology performance and usability, identifying barriers to adoption, and determining modifications needed for practical industry acceptance. 5) Conduct analyses that identify emerging hazards and future technology needs, including analysis of safety, health, injury, fatality, exposure, surveillance, operational, or other relevant data to inform future research and technology-development priorities.

description:
Le Musée national suisse (MNS) abrite une collection unique de biens culturels suisses, couvrant une période allant de la préhistoire jusqu’à nos jours. Il met en valeur ce patrimoine de manière attrayante, tant pour le public suisse que pour les visiteurs internationaux, et assure la conservation, la préservation à long terme et l’étude scientifique des objets.

Le projet d’extension a pour objectif de rassembler, sur un seul site, les dépôts et installations existants, afin de répondre à la croissance continue des besoins en surfaces.

Ce nouveau bâtiment formera, avec les structures actuelles, un ensemble cohérent d’un point de vue architectural, fonctionnel et technique.

Pendant toute la durée du chantier, les bâtiments existants resteront en service. Des mesures appropriées donc être mises en place à l’intérieur du périmètre.

Le site du projet se trouve à proximité d’infrastructures sensibles (ligne à haute tension et voie ferrée) et dans une zone archéologique. Les travaux devront être réalisés avec un soin particulier, tant sur le plan de la sécurité que dans la gestion des contraintes techniques.

title: NMAH: 2027 Install Emergency Generator
description: The Smithsonian Institution (�Smithsonian�) is providing this Notice of a Pending Solicitation for the installation of emergency generator at National Museum of American History (NMAH) 1300 Constitution Ave NW, Washington, D.C., 20560. Note: This is a revised RFP. Do not use previous posted documents from SOL# 33330226RF0010007. The applicable North American Industry Classification Codes (�NAICS�) are: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction size standard is $45.0 million. 238210 � Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors size standard is $19.0 million. Construction Budget: Over $10M. Project Information: The purpose of the NMAH: Install Emergency Generator project is to replace an aging 300 kW diesel-fueled generator located on the museum�s lower level, which has exceeded its operational lifespan. This will be accomplished by furnishing and installing two (2) new 500kW natural gas-fueled generators, on the roof adjacent to the existing emergency generator. The project also includes all necessary work to support the installation, including routing a new natural gas line through the building, and performing all associated structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, security, hazardous material abatement, and architectural modifications required to ensure full functionality, seamless integration with existing systems, and future serviceability and maintenance. Specifically, work under this project includes but is not limited to: a. Install two (2) new natural gas powered 500kW generators with integral paralleling gear on a new rooftop structural steel platform. Convert existing collections storage space (Room 4606) to a new Emergency Electrical Room to contain a new switchboard, ATS�s, transformers and panelboards. Decommission and remove existing Diesel generator on lower level. b. Coordination between complex existing building which will remain fully operational and open to the public during the duration of the work and new electrical and gas service pathways throughout. c. Existing conditions documentation early in the construction phase for implementation into BIM models. d. Development of coordination and construction BIM models early in the construction phase that depict existing conditions and proposed service pathways to enable the short circuit Study. e. A short circuit study of the proposed project prior to equipment submittals. f. Protection of existing finishes in the areas of work. g. Installation of a new gas line throughout the building to the roof to serve the new generators, including a quality control in situ mock-up. h. Installation of new conduit, MI cabling, panelboards, and pull-boxes throughout the building. Removal of existing conduit, panelboards, and pull-boxes throughout the building. i. Working around existing IT/Fiber Optic within the 4th floor corridors to allow for new conduit installation. j. Two switchover events: One from existing to temporary emergency power supplies and one for temporary to new emergency power supplies. k. Reinforcement of existing structure to support the new generators. l. Removal of the existing diesel generator in the lower level. m. Testing for lead and asbestos on existing piping at new points of connection. n. Mechanical work in the lower level to provide new fuel oil pumps. o. Work within and adjacent to sensitive Collection Storage areas that will have access restrictions and will require security escort. p. Work within and adjacent to sensitive 5th floor spaces including the Library and the Director�s Suite. q. All work is within an operational Museum with both staff and the public present. r. Ceiling removals and installation on the 4th and 5th floors. s. Hot-work required to weld the gas and containment pipe sections, cutting of existing pipe, and heat producing hot applied roofing membrane. t. Erection of temporary construction safety barriers, dust and debris air filtration and localized welding fume extraction. u. Integration and coordination of new mechanical and generator control systems into existing Siemens BAS. v. Initial testing, commissioning and black start of new electrical emergency generator systems. The museum will be open to visitors, and area adjacent to the construction site may remain open to visitors and staff. Construction Schedule: Total period of performance allowed for construction is 680 calendar days from the Notice to Proceed. This is not the requst for Proposals. The full solicitation, request for proposals and supporting documents will be released on or about beginning of December 2026; however, there is no guarantee or implication of a guarantee this this project will be solicited. Electronic copies will be uploaded to SAM.gov site. This notice does not oblige the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. DO NOT SUBMIT ANY DOCUMENTS.

buyer: Sihltal Zürich Uetliberg Bahn SZU AG
title: Switzerland – Railways traffic-control equipment – PES Sicherungsanlagen
description: Die Sihltal Zürich Uetliberg Bahn SZU AG beabsichtigt im Rahmen des Programms ERTMS SZU (PES), die bestehenden Sicherungsanlagen zu erneuern und die Voraussetzungen für die Einführung der Führerstandssignalisierung auf Basis von ETCS Level 2 zu schaffen. Ausgangslage / installierte Basis Die SZU betreibt heute auf ihrem Netz bestehende Relaisstellwerke der Typen Do55, DoC, Do67 und Do69. Die bestehenden Anlagen sollen im Rahmen von PES durch eine moderne elektronische Sicherungsanlage mit ETCS Level 2 / RBC ersetzt werden. Das derzeitige SA-Konzept bildet die Planungsgrundlage für das Mengengerüst der zukünftigen Anlage. Der aktuelle Planungsstand umfasst voraussichtlich und approximativ insbesondere, aber nicht abschliessend: · 236 EHS; · 32 Bahnübergänge; · 74 Weichen; · 291 ETCS-Balisen; · 291 Achszähler / Gleisstromkreise, vor Berücksichtigung der teilweise erforderlichen Redundanz; · 233 Gleisfreimeldeabschnitte; · 59 ERS; · 11 Rangiertafeln; · 4 CAB-Tafeln. Das Mengengerüst entspricht dem aktuellen Stand der Planung und dient als Grundlage für die Angebotserstellung. Es kann im Rahmen der weiteren Projektierung und Systemoptimierung angepasst werden. Das detaillierte Mengengerüst sowie die zugrunde liegenden Annahmen sind in der Leistungsbeschreibung und im SA-Konzept beschrieben. Gegenstand der Ausschreibung / Grundauftrag Gegenstand der vorliegenden Ausschreibung ist als Grundauftrag die Planung, Lieferung, Integration, Prüfung, Inbetriebnahme, Instandhaltung und Dokumentation der für die Einführung von ETCS Level 2 erforderlichen elektronischen Stellwerke sowie des Radio Block Centre (RBC). Die ausgeschriebenen Kernsysteme sind als integrierte Gesamtlösung zu realisieren und in die bestehende sowie zukünftige Systemlandschaft der SZU einzubinden. Der Lieferant übernimmt innerhalb der definierten Systemgrenzen die technische und funktionale Integrationsverantwortung. Dies umfasst insbesondere die Integration von Stellwerk und RBC sowie die Koordination und Sicherstellung der definierten Schnittstellen zu angrenzenden Systemen und Leistungen. Zum Grundauftrag gehören neben der Lieferung der Systeme insbesondere die erforderlichen Engineering- und Projektierungsleistungen, Systemintegration, Konfiguration, Prüfungen und Tests, Unterstützung der Sicherheitsnachweisführung und Zulassung, Migration und Inbetriebnahme sowie die für Betrieb und Unterhalt erforderliche Dokumentation und Schulung. Optionale Leistungen Zusätzlich zum Grundauftrag werden insbesondere folgende Leistungen als Optionen ausgeschrieben: · ETCS-Balisen und zugehörige Komponenten; · Achszähler bzw. Systeme zur Gleisfreimeldung; · Bahnübergangsanlagen. Die optionalen Leistungen sind durch die Anbieterin vollständig und gemäss den Ausschreibungsunterlagen zu offerieren. Die SZU ist jedoch nicht verpflichtet, diese Leistungen abzurufen und kann die Optionen einzeln oder kombiniert ausüben. Für die Angebotserstellung gelten die in den technischen Ausschreibungsunterlagen und im Preisblatt definierten Mengengerüste und Systemgrenzen. Änderungen des definitiven Mengengerüsts im Rahmen der weiteren Projektierung bleiben vorbehalten.

title: Rio De Flag - Phase 4 Construction
description: SOLICITATION W912PL27BA001: RIO DE FLAG FLOOD CONTROL PROJECT - PHASE 4 CONSTRUCTION (LOWER RDF INLET) PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): Y1KB - CONSTRUCTION OF CANALSISSUING ACTIVITY: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Los Angeles District (SPL) 1. GENERAL PROCUREMENT OVERVIEW: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Los Angeles District, is issuing this Invitation for Bids (IFB) to award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) construction contract for Phase 4 (Lower RDF Inlet) of the Rio De Flag Flood Control Project in Flagstaff, Coconino County, Arizona.- Procurement Type: Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted pursuant to FAR Part 14 and FAR Part 36 (Sealed Bidding).- Competition: Unrestricted / Full and Open Competition.- Mandatory Classification Code (PSC): Y1KB - Construction of Canals.- NAICS Code: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Small Business Size Standard: $45.0 Million).- Estimated Construction Magnitude: Between $35,000,000.00 and $50,000,000.00 (FAR 36.204).- Period of Performance: 1,095 calendar days from issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP), which includes anticipated seasonal winter shutdowns during December and January.- Solicitation Release Date: On or about 4 December 2026.- Public Virtual Bid Opening: On or about 11 February 2027. 2. DETAILED PROJECT SCOPE AND ENGINEERING FEATURES: The Rio De Flag Flood Control Project is a vital flood risk management initiative in partnership with the City of Flagstaff (Non-Federal Sponsor) designed to manage and convey 100-year (1 percent Annual Exceedance Probability [AEP]) flood discharges from Upper Rio De Flag and Clay Avenue Wash through downtown Flagstaff into the Lower Rio De Flag channel. Phase 4 involves heavy civil, structural, and environmental construction in a dense, historic urban and active railroad corridor. Major components include:- Flood Conveyance Infrastructure: Construction across an adjusted alignment limit of approximately 4,950.58 linear feet (LF), featuring: -- 1,995 LF of Reinforced Concrete Box (RCB) culverts (single and multiple-barrel sections). -- 2,555.08 LF of riprap-lined earthen trapezoidal channel (9-inch and 21-inch stone revetment). -- 200 LF of grouted stone channel, 100.5 LF of reinforced concrete transition structures, and 100 LF of rectangular concrete channel. -- Concrete wingwalls, drop inlets, junction structures, side drainage connections (18-inch to 60-inch RCP), and outlet headwalls.- Earthwork and Controlled Rock Blasting: Mass soil excavation (approx. 85,000 plus CY), soft rock excavation (approx. 27,000 plus CY), and hard basalt rock excavation (approx. 21,000 plus CY). Hard rock excavation requires precision line drilling, specialized shoring, and controlled blasting under stringent vibration thresholds.- Active Railway Corridor Coordination: Culvert construction occurs within 15 feet of active Burlington Northern Santa Fe (BNSF) Railway mainline tracks and historic downtown structures. Real-time automated geotechnical monitoring (vibration/PPV, tiltmeters, ground settlement, inclinometers, and piezometers) and strict compliance with a mandatory BNSF License Agreement are required. Work also includes relocation of the San Francisco Street BNSF signal bungalow.- Environmental Remediation: Excavation, testing, handling, and off-site disposal of petroleum-contaminated soils, and decommissioning/removal of underground storage tanks (USTs) in historic downtown locations (including former Paramount, Fuel Bunkers, Creosote, and 5 Points sites).- Civil and Utility Support: Surface water diversion and control, complex groundwater dewatering (water tables 5 to 20 feet below pre-excavation surface), extensive City of Flagstaff utility relocations (water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage), street restoration, traffic control, security fencing, automated irrigation systems, exterior plantings, and a mandatory 12-month plant establishment period. 3. SUMMARY OF IFB / SEALED BIDDING PROCEDURES:- Unit Price CLIN Schedule: Bids must be submitted against established Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) as detailed in Section 00 10 00.- No Post-Bid Negotiations: Award will be made without discussions or negotiations pursuant to FAR 14.101 and FAR 14.408. Bids must conform in all respects to the solicitation instructions.- Virtual Bid Opening: Bids will be publicly unsealed and read aloud virtually. Specific platform login and dial-in instructions will be detailed in Section 00 21 13 and any subsequent amendments.- Basis of Award: Award will be made to the lowest-priced responsive and responsible bidder. 4. MANDATORY REGISTRATION AND WEB-ONLY DISTRIBUTION:THE GOVERNMENT INTENDS TO ISSUE THIS SOLICITATION AND ALL AMENDMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF THE INTERNET (WEB ONLY). No additional media (CD-ROMs, floppy disks, faxes, or paper copies) will be provided unless deemed necessary by the Government.- SAM.gov Access: Viewing and downloading documents requires an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov/content/home.- First-Time Users: Registration requires a SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), active SAM registration, Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN), CAGE Code, and official email address.- Subcontractor Requirements: ALL prospective prime contractors and subcontractors wishing to access solicitation files must maintain an active SAM profile.- Active Registration at Award: Offerors must maintain an active SAM registration to be eligible for award (FAR 52.204-7). For Joint Ventures (JVs), the JV entity itself must have a valid SAM registration representing the joint entity.- Electronic Invoicing: Contract payment processing will be conducted electronically through PIEE / Wide Area WorkFlow (WAWF) under DFARS 252.232-7006.- Point of Entry Responsibility: It is the sole responsibility of prospective offerors to monitor https://sam.gov/content/home and PIEE frequently for any solicitation notices, files, amendments, or schedule modifications. This procurement may be delayed, canceled, or revised at any time. 5. STATUTORY AND REGULATORY HIGHLIGHTS:- Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Small businesses are reminded that under FAR 52.219-14, the prime contractor will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities (excluding material costs). Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the 85 percent subcontract limitation.- Subcontracting Plans (FAR 52.219-9 / DFARS 252.219-7003): Unrestricted large businesses must submit an acceptable Small Business Subcontracting Plan.- Bid Guarantee (FAR 52.228-1): A bid guarantee is required in the amount of 20 percent of the bid price or $3,000,000.00, whichever is less.- Performance and Payment Bonds (FAR 52.228-15): 100 percent penal amount for both Performance (SF 25) and Payment (SF 25A) bonds within 10 days of award.- Project Labor Agreement (FAR 52.222-33 / FAR 52.222-34): Executive Order 14063 policies apply to large-scale federal construction projects of $35 Million or greater.- Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (DFARS 252.204-7025): Bidders must possess at least a CMMC Level 1 (Self) assessment entered in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) prior to award.- Prevailing Wages (FAR 52.222-6): Mandatory compliance with Davis-Bacon Construction Wage Rate Requirements. 6. buyer: Sihltal Zürich Uetliberg Bahn SZU AG
title: PES Railway Signalling Systems
description:
Sihltal Zürich Uetliberg Bahn SZU AG intends to renew its existing railway signalling systems as part of the ERTMS SZU Program (PES) and to establish the necessary conditions for the introduction of cab signalling based on ETCS Level 2.


Current Situation / Installed Base

SZU currently operates relay-based interlocking systems of the types Do55, DoC, Do67 and Do69 across its railway network. As part of PES, these existing installations are to be replaced by a modern electronic signalling system incorporating ETCS Level 2 and a Radio Block Centre (RBC).


The current signalling system concept (SA Concept) forms the planning basis for the estimated quantities of the future system. At the present planning stage, the indicative scope includes, but is not limited to, the following:

·    236 EHS;

·    32 level crossings;

·    74 points (switches);

·    291 ETCS balises;

·    291 axle counters / track circuits, before accounting for partially required redundancy;

·    233 track vacancy detection sections;

·    59 ERS;

·    11 shunting boards;

·    4 CAB boards.


These quantities reflect the current planning status and serve as the basis for the preparation of tenders. They may be adjusted during further project development and system optimisation. The detailed quantities and underlying assumptions are described in the Technical Specification and the SA Concept.


Scope of Tender / Base Contract

The scope of this tender comprises, as the base contract, the engineering, supply, integration, testing, commissioning, maintenance and documentation of the electronic interlocking systems and the Radio Block Centre (RBC) required for the introduction of ETCS Level 2.


The core systems covered by this tender shall be implemented as a fully integrated solution and incorporated into SZU's existing and future system environment.


Within the defined system boundaries, the supplier shall assume responsibility for the technical and functional integration of the systems. This includes, in particular, the integration of the electronic interlocking systems and the RBC, as well as the coordination and assurance of the defined interfaces with adjacent systems and services.


In addition to the supply of the systems, the base contract includes, in particular, all necessary engineering and design services, system integration, configuration, verification and testing, support for the preparation of safety cases and regulatory approvals, migration and commissioning, as well as the documentation and training required for operation and maintenance.


Optional Services

In addition to the base contract, the following services and systems, in particular, are included in the tender as optional items:

·    ETCS balises and associated components;

·    Axle counters and/or track vacancy detection systems;

·    Level crossing protection systems.


Tenderers shall submit complete offers for the optional services in accordance with the tender documents. However, SZU shall be under no obligation to procure these optional services and may exercise the options individually or in combination.

For the preparation of tenders, the quantities and system boundaries defined in the technical tender documents and the pricing schedule shall apply. SZU reserves the right to adjust the final quantities during further project development.

title: Brand Name National Stock Numbers: Industry Feedback Request
description: GSA's Supply Chain Management Contracting Division is seeking feedback from industry regarding the Brand Name National Stock Numbers (NSNs) published with this notice. The NSNs were established as Brand Name (BN) specific at the point they were created, and therefore the Item Purchase Descriptions (IPDs) are likewise written as BN specific. Supporting information was provided at the point of NSN/IPD creation, however in some cases that information may no longer be relevant (see FAR Part 10), and as Brand Name specific items, GSA is seeking to verify whether the need described by the IPDs can in fact only be met by the one particular manufacturer cited (the manufacturer indicated in the IPD), or whether other manufacturers� products (or brands) can be offered which can meet the requirement. In order to meet the continued need for these items on behalf of our customers, GSA will seek to add these items to contract, but during the lifecycle of the NSN, we are issuing this notice as a request to industry to provide feedback confirming or countering the requirement as described. Are these manufacturer names and part numbers, as listed in the IPDs, the only manufacturers that will meet the requirement, or are there suitable substitute manufacturer names and part numbers that can be offered to meet the requirement? Please note that supporting information must be provided by industry respondents by filling in accurately and completely, all of the designated columns, for any NSN(s) that you are seeking to comment on. To respond to this feedback request, please complete the attached excel template in the highlighted columns designated for industry feedback, along with supporting documentation for all NSNs where you indicated a viable substitute, and email them to fssi.mro-req@gsa.gov. Note that all literature must contain the NSN indicated on every page of literature submitted so that the NSN association being made is clear. Also the subject line of your email must follow this naming convention: BN NSN Industry Feedback, [Your Vendor or OEM Name]. ie, "BN NSN Industry Feedback, ABC Corporation". All NSNs with corresponding Brand Name Only manufacturer and part numbers are listed on the Brand Name attachment. To request an individual IPD, please email fssi.mro-req@gsa.gov with the following naming convention in the subject: �BN NSN Industry Feedback, IPD Request, NSN (please list NSN)� The Government will not review or consider submissions concerning NSNs that are currently included on the AbilityOne Procurement List. Such NSNs are outside the scope of this RFI. The Government will not consider submissions that rely on proprietary, export-controlled, or otherwise restricted technical data the respondent is not legally authorized to use or disclose. Respondents must ensure that all submitted information was lawfully obtained and may be provided to the Government. Please note that this is a continuous RFI, submissions can be received at anytime during the life of the RFI.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: GreenFuran Direct Allylation
description: A mild, biomass-friendly route to allylated furans Manufacturers who depend on alkyl and allylic furans can now reach these valuable ingredients through a single, low-waste step that trades cryogenic equipment, hazardous reagents and costly precious metals for gentle heating and cheap, recyclable catalysts. The GreenFuran Direct Allylation method developed by Los Alamos National Laboratory feeds on renewable, biomass-derived alcohols, produces only water as a byproduct and lifts away the catalyst by simple filtration, so operators gain a cleaner process, an easier cleanup and lower input costs at the same time. Crucially, the reaction succeeds on substituted and even multiply substituted furans that older approaches simply could not convert, opening a wider palette of products from one dependable platform. The Challenge The established ways to make alkyl furans � chiefly ortho-lithiation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation or transition-metal-catalyzed C-H functionalization � each carry serious burdens when moved beyond the bench. Ortho-lithiation demands cryogenic temperatures and pyrophoric organolithium reagents that ignite on contact with air, while Friedel-Crafts routes consume stoichiometric quantities of Lewis acids that generate large volumes of waste and complicate cleanup and metal-catalyzed methods rely on expensive metals and ligands and inaccessible starting materials. Problems Solved GreenFuran Direct Allylation answers each of those burdens with a single dehydrative reaction that couples furans and allylic alcohols directly, eliminating the separate prefunctionalization step and its associated waste while yielding only water as the byproduct. The process runs under mild conditions, needing just ambient conditions or gentle heating up to 60 degrees Celsius, and it uses simple, inexpensive and environmentally benign catalysts including aluminosilicates and metal phosphates. The solid catalyst separates cleanly by filtration or decanting, removing the difficult workup common to older routes, and the allylic alcohols themselves can be drawn from renewable feedstocks. Most importantly, the method extends reliably to substituted and polysubstituted furans bearing alkyl, aryl and fused-aryl groups as well as esters, aldehydes and ketones, reaching the very targets earlier methods could not. Advantages � Mild, safer operation that avoids cryogenic cooling and hazardous, air-sensitive reagents � Inexpensive, environmentally friendly catalysts that can be removed and recovered by simple filtration � Renewable, biomass-derived starting materials such as prenol, geraniol and phytol � Only water is produced as a byproduct, cutting waste and easing cleanup � One fewer synthetic step, because no separate preparation of the alcohol is needed � Broad reach across simple and complex furans that older methods could not convert Market Applications � Food and Beverage (flavoring agents and additives) � Personal Care and Cosmetics (fragrance and cosmetic ingredients) � Chemicals (surfactants for industrial and consumer formulations) � Agriculture and Pest Control (insecticide ingredients) TRL 3 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-27238 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. Note: This is not a call for external services for the development of this technology. https://www.lanl.gov/engage/collaboration/feynman-center/partner-with-us/licensing-technology m.lanl.gov/tech-search

title: Y1PZ--Project # 926CM3010 - Cemetery Expansion and Improvements at Washington Crossing National Cemetery
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Department of Veterans Affairs, National Cemetery Administration intends to issue a solicitation entitled, Cemetery Expansion and Improvement Project, Project # 926CM3010, at the Washington Crossing National Cemetery, on or about December 20, 2026, unless additional notice is given, or this notice is modified or cancelled, the full solicitation, specifications and drawings will be posted on Contract Opportunities at beta.sam.gov. Project will include, but not limited to, extensive excavation, grading, stormwater and utility infrastructure, roads, curbs, paving, irrigation and controls, columbarium construction, manufacturing and installation of approximately 8,500 pre-placed crypt units, and repairs/renovations to the Public Information Center and maintenance building. The acquisition type for this solicitation will be Request for Proposal IAW FAR 15.101-1: Tradeoff Process. Per VAAR 836.204 Disclosure of the magnitude of construction projects, the construction magnitude for this requirement is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. The NAICS is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the business size standard is $45 Million. A site visit shall be in the month of January 2026. A date will be published in the solicitation. This procurement is 100% Set-Aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns. Only verified SDVOSB firms are eligible to submit an offer or receive an award of a VA contract that is set-aside for SDVOSB in accordance with VAAR Part 819. A non-verified vendor that submits a bid or proposal will be rejected as non-responsive. To be eligible for award, the SDVOSB must be considered small under the relevant NAICS code and must be registered and verified in the following websites: those desiring to receive an award from this solicitation must be registered at www.vetbiz.gov. Companies must have the Certified Veteran Enterprise (CVE) seal on their registration to be considered for an award. The SBA database will be checked both upon receipt of an offer and prior to award; firms must be currently registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at www.sam.gov and have completed online Representations and Certifications prior to contract award. Offers received from concerns that are not Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns shall not be considered. SDVOSBs must be verified for ownership and control and listed on Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) prior to the due date for proposals and pending award. (See VAAR Clause 852.219-10 VA Notice of Total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside.) You must register as at the SAM.gov website for the solicitation. In order to receive e-mail notification of amendments, you must register at https://secure.login.gov/?request_id=98e1f875-8f0d-4fac-a0fa-34cfb3df818b. title: M231/M232A2, Modular Artillery Charge System (MACS) Load, Assemble, and Pack (LAP)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Rock Island at Picatinny (ACC-RI-PICA), Picatinny Arsenal, New Jersey 07806-5000, on behalf of the Office of the Project Manager for Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), intends to issue competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) for the manufacture, Load, Assemble, and Pack (LAP), and final delivery of the 155MM M231 and M232 TYPE Modular Artillery Charge System (MACS) Propelling Charges. The MACS M231/M232 Type LAP meets the U.S. Army�s requirements for 155mm artillery propelling charges that are critical for and compatible with all existing 155mm artillery weapons systems and compliant with the Joint Ballistic memorandum of understanding. The 155mm M231/M232 MACS provides U.S. field artillery with a less-sensitive improved solid propelling charge system for use with current and future 155mm howitzer systems. The MACS is an evolution of the XM230 Unicharge, which was developed as a replacement for the family of four separate bag charges for the 155mm cannon artillery systems. The Unicharge was intended to be a single increment universal charge module that would provide needed zoning solutions for both 39-caliber and Extended Range Ordnance Assembly cannons by building up the charge. The MACS is currently a two-charge propellant system that offers improvement in operational flexibility, performance, logistic support, and cost when compared to the previous generation of bag propelling charges. The MACS LAP consists of two types of propelling charges, the M231 and the M232 TYPE, and all associated packaging. It uses a "build-a-charge," incremental-based system; the M231 is used singularly or in pairs for Low Zones (1 & 2) and the M232-Series is used in groups of 3, 4 or 5 charges for High Zones (3, 4 & 5). The system is compatible with all current 155mm field artillery weapons. The total maximum contract value will be $2,586,684,823.02, to include all contract awards, to procure up to an estimated 3,544,182 M231 and an estimated 15,000,000 M232 TYPE propelling charges. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database by accessing the SAM web site at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for contract award and all correspondence must be in English. Estimated time for release of the solicitation is Quarter 2, FY27 (Q2FY27). However, if any interested sources intend to review, respond, and/or submit a response to the formal Solicitation; a DRAFT Solicitation is readily available to be provided via DOD SAFE, upon request. The MACS LAP of the 155mm M231 and the M232 TYPE Propelling Charges will be in accordance with Government Technical Data Packages (TDPs). The TDPs are coded as Distribution Statement D (Further Distribution authorized to the Department of War (DoW) and U.S. DoD contractors only. Other requests for this document must be referred to the controlling DoW office: PM CAS) and will be made available once the Solicitation has been released for this effort. A completed Military Critical Technical Data Agreement (AMSTA-AR Form 1350), and a completed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) will be required prior to consideration to receiving the TDP. The POCs for any questions, DRAFT Solicitation, or the TDP request, this notification, and any requests/questions may be directed to Ms. Arian Sommers, at arian.r.sommers.civ@army.mil and Ms. Jennifer Hughes, at jennifer.m.hughes56.civ@army.mil. title: Simulator Collection for Atomic to Continuum Scales (SCACS)
description: Engineers designing semiconductors, fusion reactors, spacecraft and advanced electronics need to know how heat and electricity will move through materials, at every microscopic location where a defect, grain boundary or interface could trigger failure. SCACS, developed by scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory, delivers that insight by connecting two worlds that have long been disconnected: the atomic-scale physics that governs true material behavior and the continuum-scale engineering models used to design real devices. Built on novel atomic-site-projected conductivity methods and accelerated through graph neural networks, SCACS predicts spatially varying, direction-dependent thermal and electrical transport across large million-atom systems, giving material design Engineers a physics-grounded view of where hot-spots will form in materials, how defects will steer current and which microstructural choices will make or break performance. Overview The SCACS Toolkit is an AI-driven multiscale simulation platform designed to accelerate the development and deployment of advanced materials. Today, materials innovation is slowed by a fundamental gap: High-fidelity physics models (e.g., molecular dynamics) are too computationally expensive for real-world design, while the engineering-scale tools rely on simplified assumptions that limit predictive accuracy. This disconnect leads to costly trial-and-error development cycles and unexpected material failures in critical systems. SCACS bridges this gap by embedding machine-learned physics directly into engineering-scale simulations. Its core technology uses proprietary models Site-Projected Thermal Conductivity (SPTC-AI) and Site-Projected Electronic Conductivity (SPEC-AI) to translate first-principles insights into spatially resolved transport properties that can be used within standard finite element workflows. This approach enables accurate prediction of heat and electrical behavior in complex, heterogeneous materials at practical scales. The platform has broad commercial relevance across industries where thermal and electrical performance are critical, including semiconductors, energy systems, and advanced manufacturing. By reducing development time, improving reliability and lowering testing costs, SCACS offers a pathway to faster material qualification and more efficient product design, positioning it as a high-impact enabling technology for next-generation hardware innovation. Technology Description At its core, SCACS is a computational suite that links atomistic simulations to continuum finite-element models through two integrated modules: SPTC-AI for thermal transport and SPEC-AI for electronic transport. The Site-Projected Thermal Conductivity (SPTC) and Space-Projected Electronic Conductivity (SPEC) methods decompose a material�s bulk conductivity into per-atom contributions, revealing how individual phases, defects and interfaces locally steer the flow of heat or charge. A machine-learning graph neural network then learns these atomic-scale contributions from a curated training set and scales the predictions up to representative volume elements suitable for finite-element analysis. The companion solver modules called sptc2fem and spec2fem, built on FEniCSx, ingests the resulting thermal and electronic conductivity fields, respectively, and produces temperature/current maps, heat-flux/current density distributions and direction-resolved effective conductivities under realistic boundary conditions. This result preserves the atomic-scale anisotropy upstream that other methods would wash out. The end-to-end workflow delivers atomistic fidelity at device-relevant length scales. HPC runtimes drop from days to seconds, hot-spots and localized transport pathways become visible at the design stage, and engineers can interrogate how microstructural features will influence thermal and electrical performance before a single component is fabricated. By coarse-graining atom-resolved conductivity into spatially varying fields rather than collapsing them to a single bulk value, the technology preserves the heterogeneity, interfaces and defect populations that conventional finite-element treatments tend to hide behind an averaged scalar input. Advantages Reveals localized hot-spots and transport pathways that conventional continuum models routinely miss Cuts simulation runtimes from days on high-performance computing clusters down to minutes, without sacrificing atomic-scale fidelity Scales predictions from small atomistic cells up to million-atom microstructures previously out of reach for direct atomistic methods Captures anisotropy and spatial variation in both thermal and electrical conductivity, giving engineers a directionally accurate picture of material behavior Easily integrates with exiting finite-element solvers, such as Abaqus Market Applications Semiconductor advanced packaging (3D integrated circuits, chiplet thermal management, package reliability analysis) Fusion energy systems (divertor and first-wall plasma-facing components, refractory metal joining qualification) Aerospace and space systems (spacecraft thermal analysis, radiation-exposed materials, mission reliability modeling) Computer-aided engineering software (constitutive model inputs for industry-standard simulation platforms) Battery and energy storage (thermal management of cells, modules and packs) Thermoelectrics and biosensors (materials discovery, device-level transport characterization) Quantum device manufacturing (cryogenic cooling design, qubit thermal isolation) Related Software T5032 - SCACS is a physics-informed ML, graph neural network trained on atomic site-resolved SPTC data, enabling transfer of atomic-scale physics to device-scale modeling. title: Autonomous Ion Mass Spectrometer Sentry (AIMSS)
description: Satellite measurements of plasma density and temperature help predict the intensity of geomagnetic storms, which can impact satellites, communications, and power systems. Accurate forecasting requires knowledge of plasma composition. However, typical orbital mass spectrometers have difficulty distinguishing between nitrogen (N+) and oxygen (O+) ions due to their similar masses. This limitation makes it difficult to validate modern space weather models, which depend on accurate knowledge of ion composition in near-Earth space. N+ and O+ ions behave differently in space due to differences in their origin, transport, and loss mechanisms. Improving our ability to distinguish between these ions is critical for understanding and predicting space weather. Advantages High mass resolution enables distinction between ion species that are typically unresolved in space-based measurements (e.g., N+ vs O+) Simultaneous measurement of multiple ion species for improved data collection efficiency Commandable ion throughput allows for high dynamic range without detector saturation Flight-qualified design with near-term on-orbit demonstration on the ISS Technology Description The AIMSS instrument uses electric and magnetic fields to sort ions first by energy and then by mass. As ions move through the instrument, different species are separated and spread out across the detector as a spectrum, similar to how a prism separates white light into different colors. First, incoming ions pass through two electrostatic energy filters (ESAs) located at the front of the sensor. These filters allow only ions within a selected energy range to continue through the instrument. By adjusting the voltage applied to each filter, AIMSS can control how many ions reach the detector and adapt to changing plasma density. Next, the ions enter a magnetic field section that separates them by mass. Lighter ions are deflected more than heavier ions, causing different ion species to land at different positions on the detector. The detector records where ions land, allowing the instrument to measure multiple ion species at once and determine their mass and energy. This design achieves clear separation of closely spaced ion species such as N+ and O+, improving the accuracy of plasma composition measurements. Market Applications AIMSS supports both scientific and operational markets: Space Domain Awareness: ?Monitoring plasma density and composition to attribute spacecraft anomalies and charging events. Space Weather Monitoring and Forecasting?: Ion composition measurements of ionospheric plasma to inform space weather models and improve forecasting. Space Station Operations for Lunar and Mars Missions?: Monitoring spacecraft health, contamination, and charging during extravehicular activities (EVAs) and docking operations. Department of Defense / Space Force?: Compliance with requirements for onboard space environment sensors. title: Henkilökohtaisen avun ja muiden kotona asumista tukevien palveluiden hankinta dynaamisessa hankintajärjestelmässä
description: Tällä osallistumispyynnöllä perustetaan sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluiden dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä. Palvelun tilaajana on Keski-Uudenmaan sote-kuntayhtymä, johon kuuluvat Hyvinkään ja Järvenpään kaupungit sekä Mäntsälän, Nurmijärven, Pornaisten ja Tuusulan kunnat. Hankintajärjestelmässä hankinnan kohteena on henkilökohtaisen avun palvelut, tukihenkilöpalvelut ja vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyö. Hankinnan kohde ja hankintajärjestelmän toiminta on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän periaatteet. Palvelut on tarkoitettu Keski-Uudenmaan sote-kuntayhtymän asiakkaille, joilla on vammaisuuteen tai pitkäaikaissairauteen liittyvä tuen tarve. Palveluntuottajat voivat hakeutua hankintajärjestelmään perustamisvaiheessa ja myöhemmin sen voimassaoloaikana jättämällä osallistumishakemuksen osallistumispyynnön mukaisesti. Hankintayksikkö varaa dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän perustamisvaiheessa 25.3.2021 klo 10.00 mennessä saapuneiden osallistumishakemusten käsittelyyn 15 työpäivää. Hankintayksikkö lähettää ensimmäisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisen tarjouspyynnön luokassa 1 Henkilökohtaisen avun palvelut. Palvelun sisältö on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä Palvelukuvaus Henkilökohtaisen avun palvelut. Tarjouspyyntö lähetetään vasta kun ainakin kaikki edellä ilmoitettuun määräaikaan mennessä saapuneet osallistumishakemukset on käsitelty. Osallistumishakemukset perustamisvaiheessa tulee jättää 25.3.2021 klo 10.00 mennessä. Luokka 1 Henkilökohtaisen avun palvelut Hankinnan kohteena on henkilökohtaisen avun palvelu. Henkilökohtaisen avun palvelu perustuu vammaispalvelulain (380/1987) 8 § (vammaisille tarkoitetut palvelut), 8 c § (henkilökohtainen apu) ja 8 d §:ään (henkilökohtaisen avun järjestämistavat). Henkilökohtaisella avulla tarkoitetaan tässä laissa vaikeavammaisen henkilön välttämätöntä avustamista kotona ja kodin ulkopuolella päivittäisissä toimissa, työssä ja opiskelussa, harrastuksissa, yhteiskunnallisessa osallistumisessa tai sosiaalisen vuorovaikutuksen ylläpitämisessä. Henkilökohtaisen avun tarkoitus on auttaa vaikeavammaista henkilöä toteuttamaan omia valintojaan. Henkilökohtaisen avun järjestäminen edellyttää, että vaikeavammaisella henkilöllä on voimavaroja määritellä avun sisältö ja toteutustapa. Palveluun kuuluu asiakkaan avustaminen sellaisissa kotioloissa tehtävissä hoitotoimenpiteissä ja lääkehuollossa, jotka asiakas voisi ilman vamman tai sairauden aiheuttamaa rajoitetta tehdä itse. Palveluun kuuluu tarvittaessa asiakkaan terveydentilan seuranta. Hankinnan kohteena on henkilökohtaisen avun palvelu ostopalveluna. Hankinnan kohde kuvataan tarkemmin hankintajärjestelmän sisäisen kilpailutuksen liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa. Luokka 2 Tukihenkilöpalvelu Hankinnan kohteena on tukihenkilöpalvelu. Tukihenkilöpalvelua voidaan järjestää vammaispalvelulain 8 §: (vammaisille tarkoitetut palvelut), kehitysvammalain 2 §:n tai sosiaalihuoltolain 16 §:n (sosiaaliohjaus), 17 §:n (sosiaalinen kuntoutus) tai 28 §:n (muut sosiaalipalvelut) perusteella. Tukihenkilöpalvelun tehtävänä on asiakkaan itsenäisen toimintakyvyn tukeminen ja hyvinvoinnin ja edistäminen. Palvelu vahvistaa asiakkaan toimintakykyä ja osallisuutta kaikilla elämän osa-alueilla. Sen tehtävänä on edistää ja tukea asiakkaan itsenäistä suoriutumista ja itsemääräämistä asiakkaan yksilöllisen tarpeen mukaisella tavalla. Palvelu voi olla osana laajempaa palvelukokonaisuutta tai toteutua yksinomaisena. Tukihenkilöpalvelulla tuetaan esimerkiksi asumista, liikkumista, arjen toimintoja, asiointia, sosiaalista vuorovaikutusta, palvelujen käyttämistä, opiskelua tai työssäkäyntiä ja muita vastaavia asioita. Palveluun kuuluu asiakkaan avustaminen sellaisissa kotioloissa tehtävissä hoitotoimenpiteissä ja lääkehuollossa, jotka asiakas voisi ilman vamman tai sairauden aiheuttamaa rajoitetta tehdä itse. Palveluun kuuluu tarvittaessa asiakkaan terveydentilan seuranta. Tukihenkilöpalvelu voi olla valmennuksellista, jolloin sen tavoitteena voi olla uusien taitojen omaksumisen tukeminen. Hankinnan kohde kuvataan tarkemmin hankintajärjestelmän sisäisen kilpailutuksen liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa. Luokka 3 Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyö Hankinnan kohteena on vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyö. Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyö on vaativaa, asiakkaan kotona toteutuvaa palvelua, johon sisältyy yleensä kokonaisvaltainen hoito, hoiva ja asiakkaan itsenäisen toimintakyvyn tukeminen asiakkaan tarpeen mukaisesti. Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyötä voidaan järjestää vammaispalvelulain 8 §: (vammaisille tarkoitetut palvelut), kehitysvammalain 2 §:n tai sosiaalihuoltolain 17 §:n (sosiaalinen kuntoutus), 19 §:n (kotipalvelut), 20 §:n (kotihoito) perusteella tai 28 §:n (muut sosiaalipalvelut) perusteella. Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyö voi sisältää terveydenhuoltoon kuuluvia tehtäviä, joiden järjestäminen perustuu terveydenhuoltolakiin (1326/2010). Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyö järjestetään yleensä sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon ammattihenkilötyövoimalla. Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyön tehtävänä on asiakkaan kotona toteutuvan terveyden- ja sairaanhoidon toteuttaminen, itsenäisen toimintakyvyn tukeminen ja hyvinvoinnin ja edistäminen asiakkaan yksilöllisen tarpeen mukaisesti. Palvelu vahvistaa asiakkaan toimintakykyä ja osallisuutta kaikilla elämän osa-alueilla. Hoito- ja huolenpitotyöhön voi kuulua asiakkaan tarpeen mukaisessa laajuudessa terveydenhuoltolain 25 §:n tarkoittamaa kotisairaanhoitoa. Palvelun tarkoituksena on edistää ja tukea asiakkaan itsenäistä suoriutumista ja itsemääräämistä. Vammaisen asiakkaan hoito- ja huolenpitotyöllä tuetaan esimerkiksi asumista, liikkumista, arjen toimintoja, asiointia, sosiaalista vuorovaikutusta, palvelujen käyttämistä, opiskelua tai työssäkäyntiä ja muita vastaavia asioita. Hankinnan kohde kuvataan tarkemmin hankintajärjestelmän sisäisen kilpailutuksen liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa.

description: 1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT This is a Solicitation Synopsis issued by the Department of the Air Force, Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC/NIKM), Hill AFB, UT. This solicitation is for the production and delivery of flight test kit replenishment spares for the Flight Test, Telemetry, and Termination (FT3) Program. These kits directly support the Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC) Minuteman III (MMIII) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Force Development Evaluation Operational Test Launch (OTL) Program. 2. SOLE-SOURCE JUSTIFICATION The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source: The Boeing Company (CAGE: 0B0D7), located in Layton, UT, under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements). Market research, including a Sources Sought Synopsis (FA8214-25S-FT3PD) and Pre-solicitation Notice (FA821426RB004-PRESOL), concluded that Boeing is the only source with the unique technical data, specialized engineering expertise, and established manufacturing infrastructure required to meet the Government's strict performance schedules. Award to any other source would result in an estimated minimum duplication of $80M in costs and an unacceptable delay of at least three (3) years. 3. PROGRAM SCOPE & REQUIREMENTS The resulting contract is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) vehicle containing the following primary parameters: Quantity: Production and delivery of twenty-five (25) FT3 flight test kits. Delivery Schedule: Just-in-time delivery to Vandenberg Space Force Base, CA, precisely 120 days prior to scheduled Operational Test Launches (OTLs). Period of Performance: October 2027 through September 2035. Total Estimated Program Value: Approximately $955M (including potential future procurements executed under an approved Class J&A). 4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS & INTEREST This notice is not a request for competitive proposals, and a written solicitation will be issued directly to The Boeing Company. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet these requirements may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Information received will be evaluated solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responses must be submitted electronically to the Points of Contact listed below no later than the Response Deadline indicated in this posting.

description: Le présent appel d'offres porte sur des prestations d'entrepreneur général en Suisse alémanique, romande et italienne sous forme d'un contrat-cadre. La durée du contrat est de trois ans, avec une option de prolongation de deux ans supplémentaires. Marché spécifique pour le nettoyage du ballast (SR) des voies (hors aiguillages) à écartement normal. Le soumissionnaire doit être en mesure de réaliser les projets de renouvellement de la voie en tant qu’entrepreneur général (EG). En règle générale, l’attribution du mandat intervient à partir de la phase partielle SIA 51 (projet d’exécution). Dans certains cas, l’implication préalable de l’entreprise est nécessaire afin d’établir la planification des phases de construction pendant les phases partielles 31-33. Il n’existe aucune obligation d’achat pour CFF SA (aucune prétention quant à l’atteinte du montant du contrat d’ici à la fin de la durée contractuelle, option comprise). Contenu de ces lots : Type/genre : Lot spécial pour le criblage de ballast (SR) des voies (hors appareils de voie), à l'échelle de la Suisse. Réalisation en tant qu'entrepreneur général. Description : Lot SR spécialisé pour des projets ferroviaires (hors appareils de voie) à écartement normal, d'une longueur comprise entre environ 1 000 m et 9 000 m maximum. Aucun appareil de voie doit être modifié. Aucun ouvrage de génie civil majeur, tel que des soutènements d'accotements ou des systèmes de drainage, ne doit être réalisé. Particularités : La prestation de « criblage du ballast » dans des conditions d'espace restreint avec une largeur de passage < 320 cm ne doit pas nécessairement pouvoir être fournie (prestation facultative). Aucun remplacement du ballast ni aucune remise en état de la plateforme ferroviaire ne doivent être effectués. Les modifications des appareils de voie ne sont pas incluses et ne doivent pas être réalisées. Aucun travail principal de génie civil ne doit être réalisé (prestation facultative). Prestations facultatives : Le remplacement du ballast (SE) sur les voies ferrées peut être effectué par une entreprise sur une base volontaire à proposer également (pas d'UBS, pas d'aiguillages). Les travaux principaux de génie civil peuvent être proposés à titre facultatif. Volume/Quantité : Volume annuel d'environ 20 à 40 km de nettoyage de ballast. Quantité minimale d'achat garantie de 20 km/an. Le volume annuel théorique maximal correspond au double de la quantité minimale d'achat, soit 40 km/an de nettoyage de ballast. Cette valeur est déterminante pour le rabais de quantité. Adjudications: Une seule adjudication.

title: Y1DA--Community Living Center Phase 2 (Minor) Construction - Columbia - Project 589-404
description: Page 1 of 1 INTRODUCTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract for the Design-Bid-Build Construct Community Living Center Phase 2 (Minor) Construction project at the Harry S. Truman VA Medical Center (VAMC) located at 800 Hospital Drive, Columbia, MO 65201. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Columbia VAMC is seeking a general contractor to completely prepare site for building operations, including demolition and removal of existing structures, and furnish labor and materials and perform work for the Construct Community Living Center (CLC) Phase II. The purpose of this project is to construct the second phase of the Community Living Center. The 2nd phase will consist of a 24 bed, 20,400 square foot two story addition onto the phase 1 Community Living Center (CLC). The new construction will enable relocation of the final 24 beds out of the existing CLC in the main hospital. ADMINISTRATIVE: The solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) conducted in accordance with FAR Parts 15, 19, and 36 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be advertised as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45 million. The solicitation will be issued in December of 2026. The period of performance is approximately 790 calendar days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to: thomas.council@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted. -END-

title: Production equipment for manufacturing vehicle license plates
description:
The Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Zurich has commissioned the Pöschwies Correctional Facility in Regensdorf to manufacture cantonal vehicle license plates. To fulfill this production mandate effectively over the long term—ensuring economic viability and impeccable quality—it is necessary to procure modern production equipment, relevant system accessories, and associated services.




The subject of this tender is the selection of a capable supplier for:


Embossing presses: High-performance machines for license plate production, including necessary operational accessories.

Embossing dies and storage: Complete sets of embossing dies and suitable, organized storage systems for safe and efficient handling.

Hot-stamping machines: Specialized machines for the precise coloring of embossed license plates.

Staff training: Comprehensive training and instruction for the facility's operating personnel to ensure safe and professional operation of all equipment.

Maintenance and support (SLA): Conclusion of a Service Level Agreement to ensure ongoing maintenance, periodic inspections, and rapid troubleshooting for maximum operational reliability.



The machinery, tools, and services to be supplied must be fully suitable for the production of Swiss vehicle license plates. They must strictly comply with all applicable technical specifications and defined quality standards for Swiss license plates.




The objective of this tender is to conclude a supply contract covering delivery, installation, commissioning, and training, as well as a separate Service Level Agreement (SLA) for ongoing maintenance.

title: Belgium – Construction work – Construction de la Station d'épuration de Strée
description: Marché de travaux : Collecte des eaux urbaines résiduaires du bassin hydrographique de la Sambre. Construction de la station d’épuration de Strée. Le marché a pour objet premier les études, l'établissement des plans, la réalisation, la mise en service d'une station de traitement d’eaux usées domestiques, d’une capacité administrative équivalente à 1 125 EH pour l’épuration des eaux usées de l’entité de Strée dans la commune de Beaumont. L’implantation se fera sur le territoire de la commune de Thuin. Le contenu du marché et son contexte général d’exécution sont développés dans la partie technique du présent cahier des charges. Outre les études, les plans d'exécution, la réalisation et la mise en service de l’installation, l'entreprise a pour objet l'établissement des documents, autorisations, permis, prestations, fournitures, essais nécessaires à l'exécution des travaux, l'établissement d'un état des lieux avant et après travaux, dressé en présence du pouvoir adjudicateur ainsi que la réalisation des dossiers « après travaux » tels que décrit dans les clauses techniques. Les travaux sont situés en zone agricole soumise à aléa d’inondation faible par débordement. L’attention des soumissionnaires est attirée sur le fait que le Présent Cahier Spécial des Charges contient des clauses anti-dumping social (assorties de pénalités spéciales importantes) mises au point dans le cadre du Comité de Développement Stratégique de la Région de Charleroi et du Sud-Hainaut. Elles sont surlignées en gris dans le C.S.CH. En conséquence de quoi, les soumissionnaires sont fermement invités : - à en tenir compte dans l’élaboration de leur offre, le Pouvoir Adjudicateur se donnant les moyens de vérifier la conformité du chantier à celles-ci et de sanctionner en cas d’infraction ; - à compléter et joindre à l’offre la Déclaration sur l’honneur relative aux clauses anti-dumping social reprise en annexe du présent Cahier Spécial des Charges. L’absence de déclaration jointe à l’offre ou une déclaration jointe mais non complétée sera considérée comme révélant l’intention du non-respect des clauses contre le dumping social et, en conséquence, considérée comme une irrégularité substantielle. Le contenu du marché et son contexte général d’exécution sont développés dans la partie technique du présent cahier des charges.
